title: Lisse realization of the rationalized constructible heart, with tensor and point normalization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$, its valuation ring $R$ and a uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k$-scheme, not necessarily separated. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $\widehat R_X=\varprojlim_n(R/\varpi^n)_X$, the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and $E_X=\widehat R_X[1/\varpi]$, its localization at $\varpi$ (the sheaf colimit of repeated multiplication by $\varpi$). Let $\operatorname{Loc}(X,E_X)$ be the category of $E_X$-module sheaves pro-etale locally isomorphic to a finite direct sum of copies of $E_X$, allowing rank zero and varying finite local ranks [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the raw rationalized category $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and its standard heart [def-weil-constructible-heart].

Derived scalar extension $K\mapsto E_X\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\widehat R_X}K$ on integral representatives, with a morphism $f\otimes a$ sent to $a(1\otimes f)$, induces a fully faithful realization on the lisse subcategory of this heart, with essential image $\operatorname{Loc}(X,E_X)$ in degree zero. Here the lisse subcategory consists of objects pro-etale locally isomorphic, in the localized coefficient category, to finite sums of the coefficient unit. Thus these two lisse categories are equivalent; their Hom identifications are the ones induced by the specified scalar extension.

On lisse objects this realization identifies the coefficient unit and tensor product of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] with $E_X$ and the ordinary sheaf tensor product. For every scheme morphism $f:X'\to X$ between finite-type $k$-schemes (not required to be $k$-linear), it identifies $Lf_E^*$ on lisse objects with the ordinary module inverse image $E_{X'}\otimes_{f^{-1}E_X}f^{-1}(-)$. These comparisons are natural in sheaf maps and compatible with tensor associativity, symmetry, units, identity and composition of pullbacks, and finite coefficient-field extension. They send a pulled-back local basis vector to the same basis vector, and a pure tensor to the corresponding pure tensor. At a common finite field stage they therefore give the same assertions for lisse objects of $\Sh_c(X,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

For $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $x:s\to X$, the point fibre $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lx^*K)$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] corresponds to sections at $s$ of the ordinary pullback of the realized lisse sheaf, followed by scalar extension to $\Qlb$ when appropriate. This identification is natural and respects tensor products and their units. For an automorphism $h:s\to s$, the point-transport map constructed by restriction along $h$ and the inverse-image coprojection, as in [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], is carried to that same restriction-and-coprojection map in the $E_X$-module-sheaf model; the identification also respects its iterates.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6), Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15, pp. 58-62. Lisse restriction with explicit normalization for the completed/rationalized operations and point transport; these normalization clauses are an agent formulation of the comparison, not a verbatim theorem of the source.

proof.text: A field is noetherian. Finite type gives local noetherianity and quasi-compactness; the noetherian space has quasi-compact opens, so $X$ is qcqs. Its dimension is finite. The same applies to $X′$ and quasi-compact etale charts. The continuous coefficient identifications and exact restriction/localization assertions fix the rings and realization used below.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; assembly of the 2026-10-22 re-split, step 1

proof.text: The common integral categories agree by the stratified-perfect characterization. The constructible Hom comparison gives full faithfulness with $u\otimes a\mapsto aF(u)$. The lisse-image lemma puts its values in ordinary degree-zero sheaves; the lattice-lifting lemma supplies every finite locally free sheaf. Thus restriction gives the required equivalence with the specified Hom maps.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; assembly of the 2026-10-22 re-split, step 2

proof.text: Apply the normalized tensor and pullback comparison to integral representatives, then to localized arrows. On lisse objects its derived tensors are ordinary sheaf tensors in degree zero. Its formulas identify the unit, pure tensors and pulled-back basis vectors, for arbitrary scheme maps.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; assembly of the 2026-10-22 re-split, step 3

proof.text: Apply finite scalar comparison and coherence to these very comparisons. The quotient-cone normalization identifies their finite diagrams; the asserted local-basis formulas give the tensor, symmetry, unit, identity, composition and field-extension compatibilities simultaneously.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; assembly of the 2026-10-22 re-split, step 4

proof.text: The sections-localization isomorphism at $s$ followed by the normalized pullback comparison for $x$ identifies the recorded fibre with ordinary pullback sections. Its tensor and unit assertions give the requested natural point-fibre identification.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; assembly of the 2026-10-22 re-split, step 5

proof.text: For each automorphism of $s$, the transport lemma identifies the specified completed map with restriction, coprojection and the ordinary module unit, including the formula on fractions. Its iterate assertion identifies every repeated transport with the same ordinary construction.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; assembly of the 2026-10-22 re-split, step 6

proof.text: Finally represent objects, arrows and each finite diagram over one finite coefficient field, taking composita. Apply the preceding comparisons there. Their scalar tower laws identify the maps after every further extension; equal representatives stay equal and inverse maps stay inverse. They therefore descend to the common-stage lisse category, with scalar extension of point fibres to $\Qlb$.

Repair note: released stage-1 re-split with keep_plan. Live and side-live still hold the 13-step base and no other group has re-split it. The item statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to live, and all 13 base step texts are kept verbatim in the report. Allocation: old 1 → assembly step 1 (short elementary chain). Old 2: exactness and the H^i formula → lem-tw-lisse-localization-restriction; Hom continuity and Hom localization → the existing lem-per-constructible-rational-hom-comparison. That node is stated for the PBC category, which equals def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed by lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization, and the two raw rationalizations have the same Hom ⊗ E formula. Old 3 → localization-restriction; old 4 → lattice-heart-lift; old 5–6 → tensor-pullback-realization; old 7–8 → scalar-comparison-coherence; old 9–10 → point-sections-realization; old 11–12 → point-transport-realization; old 13 → assembly step 7 (elementary, as on the base). Nothing was dropped. The six statement-only nodes are 2.5–3.3k characters each and each carries 1–2 old steps; the assembly is 2232 characters. Statements tested: A is flat over B, so F is exact; Hom between degree-zero objects is sheaf Hom; N comes from BS 6.8.13 and the étale-local lattices from BS 6.8.4(6) on finite-type charts; lifts are unique by full faithfulness, which reflects isomorphisms; χ needs a qcqs base and η needs noetherian finite-dimensional schemes, both satisfied with no k-linearity; at s = Spec k, B_s(s) = R and Γ commutes with the localization colimit; pro-étale covers of s split, so fibres are E^r. Edge cases checked: empty X, rank 0, varying ranks, E = E', f = id, h = id, r = 0. BS pp. 58–62 (6.8.2, 6.8.3, 6.8.4(6), 6.8.11(3), 6.8.12–6.8.15) were read at the cited places. No SGA is cited. No cycles. Tool uses are generic infrastructure and are accepted. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact only states that the inverse image of a geometric morphism is exact. That is neither the trace formula, Poincaré duality, nor a step of their proofs, and it was already in the base closure. The new closure adds no sec-trace-formula or sec-poincare-duality node, so the flag is accepted. Advisory: localization-restriction's first clause specializes lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor. The PBC-side Q115 nodes (lem-per-rational-realization-pullback-comparison and -scalar-coherence) are analogues but use different completed operations and carry no lisse normalizations. The report should have listed them, and provers may use them.
